text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Man dies in hospital after police beat him up in demonstration in southern city of Antalya to push the government to bring a security scandal to light.
- Parliament will vote on commission reports into corruption charges against Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller this week.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz calls on Justice Minister Sevket Kazan to resign because he visited an Islamist former mayor in jail for holding an anti-Israel rally.
- Parents protest at education ministry's decision to stop teaching in foreign languages at top-grade high schools.
- President Suleyman Demirel says Turkey's secularist structure cannot be called into question.
- More than 14 million Turks are at risk of having a heart attack, a survey reveals.
- Leather industry asks for immediate measures to be taken to combat competition from Italy, Dubai and China.
- A report by the National Security Council calls for lessons in "anti-terrorism" to be taught in schools.
